statement: Using the change-of-base formula, show that $\log_{2}3\cdot\log_{3}4=\log_{2}4$ and evaluate it.
solution: By change of base, $\log_{a}b=\dfrac{\ln b}{\ln a}$. Hence $\log_{2}3\cdot\log_{3}4=\dfrac{\ln 3}{\ln 2}\cdot\dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln 3}=\dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln 2}=\log_{2}4=2$. More generally $\log_{a}b\cdot\log_{b}c=\log_{a}c$.
hints: Write each logarithm as a ratio of natural logs.
